newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Bilbao wants 100 pct of Credito Argentino - reports.
newsitem.headline: Bilbao wants 100 pct of Credito Argentino - reports.

text.p: Spain's Banco de Bilbao Vizcaya said its controlled Banco Frances in Argentina, which has signed a deal to buy control of Banco de Credito Argentino, wants to buy all Credito's shares, according to local media Wednesday.
"In the case Santibanez sells, we buy and get 100 percent of BC (Credito)," Gonzalo Terrero, in charge of BBV's business in Latin America, was quoted as saying by La Nacion newspaper.
He referred to the remaining 28 percent stake shareholder Fernando de Santibanez has in Credito, which Friday signed a deal to sell a 71.8 percent stake to Frances for $466 million.
Analysts have said they considered a price of up to $450 million to be reasonable.

Banco de Balibao representative Pedro Uriarte told El Cronista newspaper that for Santibanez "the decision is as easy as throwing a coin into the air: He sells his stake or he swaps it for Frances's shares and, in that case, he would be left with a nine percent stake in the merged bank."
Uriarte added Bilbao plans no layoffs or branch closures once the merger of the two Argentine banks takes place.
"We are not thinking about staff reductions or branch closures," he said, according to El Cronista.
Analysts had said that the merger would result in branch-overlapping and that closures would be necessary.
Frances is Argentina's third largest private bank after Banco de Galicia and Rio, while Credito is one of Argentina's 10 top retail banks, with a net worth of $305 million.
Frances clients are mainly big companies and high income individuals while Credito is more a retail bank with strong presence in the mid-to-low income segment.

Frances' business is "absolutely complementary" with that of Credito's, Uriarte said according to El Cronista. "The resulting company will be better and more universal than the two sides taking part in the merger."

Frances will carry out a $300-$350 million capital increase to finance the purchase, the state-run Telam news agency quoted an unnamed representative of Bilbao's as saying Tuesday. But Frances Marketing Manager Guillermo Laje called the report premature.
Analysts say the deal is a strategic move by Bilbao to widen its retail business in Latin America, where it already has a retail presence in countries like Mexico, Colombia and Peru.
